name: Q₈
notes: Hamilton's quaternions, 1843 — the eight units of a number system he spent thirteen years looking for, then carved into Broom Bridge in Dublin when it came to him on a walk. The arrows were extracted from quaternion algebra (i²=j²=k²=-1; ijk cycles forward positive, backward negative); that extraction is Hamilton's domain, not group theory. What makes it worth studying HERE: it is only the second non-abelian group met, it needs two generators because ⟨i⟩ reaches just four of the eight, and it is one of exactly two non-abelian groups of order 8 — D₄ being the other. Unusually, every one of its subgroups is normal, which is rare enough to have its own name: a Hamiltonian group. Carter writes it Q₄; most sources write Q₈. Same group.
source: extracted from quaternion algebra — Carter, Visual Group Theory, exercise 4.6(b)
